CREATE TABLE cards (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    asciiName TEXT -- Column Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.,
    availability TEXT -- Column Description: A list of the card's available printing types., Column Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar",
    borderColor TEXT -- Column Description: The color of the card border., Column Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white",
    cardKingdomFoilId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Foil Id, Column Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.,
    cardKingdomId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Id, Column Value Explanation: A list of all the colors in the color indicator,
    colorIdentity TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text,
    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    colors TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator., Column Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.,
    convertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana,
    duelDeck TEXT -- Column Description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.,
    edhrecRank INTEGER -- Column Description: The card rank on EDHRec,
    faceConvertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face,
    faceName TEXT -- Column Description: The name on the face of the card.,
    flavorName TEXT -- Column Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.,
    frameEffects TEXT -- Column Description: The visual frame effects., Column Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc",
    frameVersion TEXT -- Column Description: The version of the card frame style., Column Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future",
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size => +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size => -1, .... neural maximum hand size => 0....,
    hasAlternativeDeckLimit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck., Column Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow,
    hasContentWarning INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,
    hasFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    hasNonFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in non-foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    isAlternative INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing, Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is only available in online game variations., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isOversized INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is oversized., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isPromo INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is a promotional printing., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isReprint INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has been reprinted., Column Value Explanation: 0: has not 1: has not been,
    isReserved INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window), Column Value Explanation: If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List,
    isStarter INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isStorySpotlight INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is a Story Spotlight card., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isTextless INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card does not have a text box., Column Value Explanation: 0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;,
    isTimeshifted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is time shifted, Column Value Explanation: If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion.,
    keywords TEXT -- Column Description: A list of keywords found on the card.,
    layout TEXT -- Column Description: The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token",
    leadershipSkills TEXT -- Column Description: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in,
    life TEXT -- Column Description: The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.,
    loyalty TEXT -- Column Description: The starting loyalty value of the card., Column Value Explanation: Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown,
    manaCost TEXT -- Column Description: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value., Column Value Explanation: manaCost is unconverted mana cost,
    mcmId TEXT,
    mcmMetaId TEXT,
    mtgArenaId TEXT,
    mtgjsonV4Id TEXT,
    mtgoFoilId TEXT,
    mtgoId TEXT,
    multiverseId TEXT,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the card., Column Value Explanation: Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.,
    number TEXT -- Column Description: The number of the card,
    originalReleaseDate TEXT -- Column Description: original Release Date, Column Value Explanation: The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions.,
    originalText TEXT -- Column Description: original Text, Column Value Explanation: The text on the card as originally printed.,
    originalType TEXT -- Column Description: original Type, Column Value Explanation: The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    otherFaceIds TEXT -- Column Description: other Face Ids, Column Value Explanation: A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces.,
    power TEXT -- Column Description: The power of the card., Column Value Explanation: ∞ means infinite power / null or * refers to unknown power,
    printings TEXT -- Column Description: A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.,
    promoTypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of promotional types for a card., Column Value Explanation: "arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork",
    purchaseUrls TEXT -- Column Description: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.,
    rarity TEXT -- Column Description: The card printing rarity.,
    scryfallId TEXT,
    scryfallIllustrationId TEXT,
    scryfallOracleId TEXT,
    setCode TEXT -- Column Description: The set printing code that the card is from.,
    side TEXT -- Column Description: The identifier of the card side., Column Value Explanation: Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card.,
    subtypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.,
    supertypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash., Column Value Explanation: list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes,
    tcgplayerProductId TEXT,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The rules text of the card.,
    toughness TEXT -- Column Description: The toughness of the card.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes., Column Value Explanation: "Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant",
    types TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.,
    uuid TEXT NOT NULL -- Column Description: The universal unique identifier (v5) generated by MTGJSON. Each entry is unique.,
    variations TEXT,
    watermark TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the watermark on the card.,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE foreign_data (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id number identifying this row of data,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign flavor text of the card.,
    language TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign language of card.,
    multiverseid INTEGER -- Column Description: The foreign multiverse identifier of the card.,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign name of the card.,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign text ruling of the card.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign type of the card. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    uuid TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_foreign_data_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE legalities (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this legality,
    format TEXT -- Column Description: format of play, Column Value Explanation: each value refers to different rules to play,
    status TEXT -- , Column Value Explanation: legal / banned /restricted,
    uuid TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_legalities_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE rulings (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this ruling,
    date DATE -- Column Description: date,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: description about this ruling,
    uuid TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_rulings_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE set_translations (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this set,
    language TEXT -- Column Description: language of this card set,
    setCode TEXT -- Column Description: the set code for this set,
    translation TEXT -- Column Description: translation of this card set,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_set_translations_setCode FOREIGN KEY (setCode) REFERENCES sets (code)

);

CREATE TABLE sets (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this set,
    baseSetSize INTEGER -- Column Description: The number of cards in the set.,
    block TEXT -- Column Description: The block name the set was in.,
    booster TEXT -- Column Description: A breakdown of possibilities and weights of cards in a booster pack.,
    code TEXT NOT NULL -- Column Description: The set code for the set.,
    isFoilOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is only available in foil.,
    isForeignOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is available only outside the United States of America.,
    isNonFoilOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is only available in non-foil.,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is only available in online game variations.,
    isPartialPreview INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is still in preview (spoiled). Preview sets do not have complete data.,
    keyruneCode TEXT -- Column Description: The matching Keyrune code for set image icons.,
    mcmId INTEGER -- Column Description: The Magic Card Marketset identifier.,
    mcmIdExtras INTEGER -- Column Description: The split Magic Card Market set identifier if a set is printed in two sets. This identifier represents the second set's identifier.,
    mcmName TEXT,
    mtgoCode TEXT -- Column Description: The set code for the set as it appears on Magic: The Gathering Online, Column Value Explanation: if the value is null or empty, then it doesn't appear on Magic: The Gathering Online,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the set.,
    parentCode TEXT -- Column Description: The parent set code for set variations like promotions, guild kits, etc.,
    releaseDate DATE -- Column Description: The release date in ISO 8601 format for the set.,
    tcgplayerGroupId INTEGER -- Column Description: The group identifier of the set on TCGplayer,
    totalSetSize INTEGER -- Column Description: The total number of cards in the set, including promotional and related supplemental products but excluding Alchemy modifications - however those cards are included in the set itself.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The expansion type of the set., Column Value Explanation: "alchemy", "archenemy", "arsenal", "box", "commander", "core", "draft_innovation", "duel_deck", "expansion", "from_the_vault", "funny", "masterpiece", "masters", "memorabilia", "planechase", "premium_deck", "promo", "spellbook", "starter", "token", "treasure_chest", "vanguard",
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.uuid
    FROM cards AS T1
    INNER JOIN sets AS T2
      ON T1.setCode = T2.code
    WHERE T2.name = 'Coldsnap'

This involves joining the 'cards', 'foreign_data', 'sets' and 'set_translations' tables. The set name 'Coldsnap' will filter the sets table. The language 'Italian' will filter the foreign_data and set_translations tables. The set_code columns will be used to join the tables.

CREATE TABLE cards (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    asciiName TEXT -- Column Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.,
    availability TEXT -- Column Description: A list of the card's available printing types., Column Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar",
    borderColor TEXT -- Column Description: The color of the card border., Column Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white",
    cardKingdomFoilId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Foil Id, Column Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.,
    cardKingdomId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Id, Column Value Explanation: A list of all the colors in the color indicator,
    colorIdentity TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text,
    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    colors TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator., Column Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.,
    convertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana,
    duelDeck TEXT -- Column Description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.,
    edhrecRank INTEGER -- Column Description: The card rank on EDHRec,
    faceConvertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face,
    faceName TEXT -- Column Description: The name on the face of the card.,
    flavorName TEXT -- Column Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.,
    frameEffects TEXT -- Column Description: The visual frame effects., Column Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc",
    frameVersion TEXT -- Column Description: The version of the card frame style., Column Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future",
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size => +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size => -1, .... neural maximum hand size => 0....,
    hasAlternativeDeckLimit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck., Column Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow,
    hasContentWarning INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,
    hasFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    hasNonFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in non-foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    isAlternative INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing, Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is only available in online game variations., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isOversized INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is oversized., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isPromo INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is a promotional printing., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isReprint INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has been reprinted., Column Value Explanation: 0: has not 1: has not been,
    isReserved INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window), Column Value Explanation: If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List,
    isStarter INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isStorySpotlight INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is a Story Spotlight card., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isTextless INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card does not have a text box., Column Value Explanation: 0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;,
    isTimeshifted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is time shifted, Column Value Explanation: If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion.,
    keywords TEXT -- Column Description: A list of keywords found on the card.,
    layout TEXT -- Column Description: The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token",
    leadershipSkills TEXT -- Column Description: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in,
    life TEXT -- Column Description: The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.,
    loyalty TEXT -- Column Description: The starting loyalty value of the card., Column Value Explanation: Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown,
    manaCost TEXT -- Column Description: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value., Column Value Explanation: manaCost is unconverted mana cost,
    mcmId TEXT,
    mcmMetaId TEXT,
    mtgArenaId TEXT,
    mtgjsonV4Id TEXT,
    mtgoFoilId TEXT,
    mtgoId TEXT,
    multiverseId TEXT,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the card., Column Value Explanation: Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.,
    number TEXT -- Column Description: The number of the card,
    originalReleaseDate TEXT -- Column Description: original Release Date, Column Value Explanation: The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions.,
    originalText TEXT -- Column Description: original Text, Column Value Explanation: The text on the card as originally printed.,
    originalType TEXT -- Column Description: original Type, Column Value Explanation: The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    otherFaceIds TEXT -- Column Description: other Face Ids, Column Value Explanation: A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces.,
    power TEXT -- Column Description: The power of the card., Column Value Explanation: ∞ means infinite power / null or * refers to unknown power,
    printings TEXT -- Column Description: A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.,
    promoTypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of promotional types for a card., Column Value Explanation: "arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork",
    purchaseUrls TEXT -- Column Description: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.,
    rarity TEXT -- Column Description: The card printing rarity.,
    scryfallId TEXT,
    scryfallIllustrationId TEXT,
    scryfallOracleId TEXT,
    setCode TEXT -- Column Description: The set printing code that the card is from.,
    side TEXT -- Column Description: The identifier of the card side., Column Value Explanation: Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card.,
    subtypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.,
    supertypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash., Column Value Explanation: list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes,
    tcgplayerProductId TEXT,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The rules text of the card.,
    toughness TEXT -- Column Description: The toughness of the card.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes., Column Value Explanation: "Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant",
    types TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.,
    uuid TEXT NOT NULL -- Column Description: The universal unique identifier (v5) generated by MTGJSON. Each entry is unique.,
    variations TEXT,
    watermark TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the watermark on the card.,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE foreign_data (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id number identifying this row of data,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign flavor text of the card.,

FROM sets AS T1

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the set code for 'Coldsnap' from the sets table. 2) Find the cards in this set. 3) Find the highest convertedManaCost among these cards. 4) Find the Italian names of these cards. The sets.name and set_translations.language columns are needed to filter for the set and language. The cards.convertedManaCost column is needed to find the highest converted mana cost. The foreign_data.name column is needed to retrieve the Italian card names.  The cards.setCode column is needed to join the tables.

The question asks for the Italian names of cards in the 'Coldsnap' set that have the highest converted mana cost. To achieve this, I need to join the `cards` table with the `foreign_data` table to get the Italian names and filter by the set 'Coldsnap'. I also need to find the maximum `convertedManaCost` from the `cards` table and then filter the results to include only those cards matching this maximum cost. Finally, I will select the `name` from the `foreign_data` table.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.name
FROM foreign_data AS T1
INNER JOIN cards AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
INNER JOIN sets AS T3
  ON T2.setCode = T3.code
WHERE T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.language = 'Italian' AND T2.convertedManaCost = (
  SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost)
  FROM cards AS T4
  INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T5
    ON T4.uuid = T5.uuid
  INNER JOIN sets AS T6
    ON T4.setCode = T6.code
  WHERE T6.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T5.language = 'Italian'
);

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1.name
FROM foreign_data AS T1
INNER JOIN cards AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
INNER JOIN sets AS T3
  ON T2.setCode = T3.code
WHERE
  T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.language = 'Italian' AND T2.convertedManaCost = (
    SELECT
      MAX(T2_sub.convertedManaCost)
    FROM foreign_data AS T1_sub
    INNER JOIN cards AS T2_sub
      ON T1_sub.uuid = T2_sub.uuid
    INNER JOIN sets AS T3_sub
      ON T2_sub.setCode = T3_sub.code
    WHERE
      T3_sub.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1_sub.language = 'Italian'
  );

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the Italian names of cards in the 'Coldsnap' set that have the highest converted mana cost. To achieve this, I need to join the `cards` table with the `foreign_data` table to get the Italian names and filter by the set 'Coldsnap'. I also need to find the maximum `convertedManaCost` from the `cards` table and then filter the results to include only those cards matching this maximum cost. Finally, I will select the `name` from the `foreign_data` table.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T2."name"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "foreign_data" AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."setCode" = (
    SELECT "code"
    FROM "sets"
    WHERE "name" = 'Coldsnap'
  )
  AND T1."convertedManaCost" = (
    SELECT MAX(T3."convertedManaCost")
    FROM "cards" AS T3
    WHERE T3."setCode" = (
      SELECT "code"
      FROM "sets"
      WHERE "name" = 'Coldsnap'
    )
  )
  AND T2."language" = 'Italian';

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter for mythic cards (cards.rarity = 'mythic'), 2) Find the oldest release date (MIN(cards.originalReleaseDate)), 3) Join with legalities table to get legal play formats (legalities.status = 'Legal'). The originalReleaseDate column is needed to find the oldest card. The rarity column is needed to filter for mythic cards. The format column is needed to identify the legal play formats. The status column is needed to filter for legal formats. The cards.id is needed to join with legalities. Note: id, availability, cardKingdomId, colorIdentity, duelDeck, faceName, frameEffects, hasNonFoil, isPromo, layout, life, name, number, originalText, originalType, scryfallId, scryfallOracleId, side, text, toughness, type, variations are not needed for this query.

The question asks for the release year of the oldest mythic card and its legal play formats. To find the oldest mythic card, I need to filter the 'cards' table by rarity='mythic' and then find the minimum 'originalReleaseDate'. To get the legal play formats, I need to join the 'cards' table with the 'legalities' table on the card's UUID and filter for 'status'='legal'. Finally, I need to extract the year from the 'originalReleaseDate'. Therefore, I need 'rarity' and 'originalReleaseDate' from the 'cards' table, and 'format' and 'status' from the 'legalities' table.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1."originalReleaseDate",
  T2."format"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."rarity" = 'mythic' AND T1."originalReleaseDate" = (
    SELECT
      MIN("originalReleaseDate")
    FROM "cards"
    WHERE
      "rarity" = 'mythic'
  ) AND T2."status" = 'Legal';

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1."originalReleaseDate",
  T2."format"
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."rarity" = 'mythic' AND T2."status" = 'Legal' AND T1."originalReleaseDate" = (
    SELECT
      MIN(T3."originalReleaseDate")
    FROM cards AS T3
    WHERE
      T3."rarity" = 'mythic'
  )
ORDER BY
  T2."format" ASC;

SELECT T1."originalReleaseDate", T2."format"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE T1."uuid" = (
  SELECT "uuid"
  FROM "cards"
  WHERE "rarity" = 'mythic'
  ORDER BY "originalReleaseDate" ASC NULLS LAST
  LIMIT 1
) AND T2."status" = 'Legal';

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter for mythic cards (cards.rarity = 'mythic'), 2) Find the oldest release date (MIN(cards.originalReleaseDate)), 3) Join with legalities table to get legal play formats (legalities.status = 'Legal'). The originalReleaseDate column is needed to find the oldest card. The rarity column is needed to filter for mythic cards. The format column is needed to identify the legal play formats. The status column is needed to filter for legal formats. The cards.id is needed to join with legalities. Note: id, availability, cardKingdomId, colorIdentity, duelDeck, faceName, frameEffects, hasNonFoil, isPromo, layout, life, name, number, originalText, originalType, scryfallId, scryfallOracleId, side, text, toughness, type, variations are not needed for this query.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1."originalReleaseDate",
  T2."format"
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."rarity" = 'mythic' AND T2."status" = 'Legal' AND T1."originalReleaseDate" = (
    SELECT
      MIN(T3."originalReleaseDate")
    FROM cards AS T3
    WHERE
      T3."rarity" = 'mythic'
  )
ORDER BY
  T2."format" ASC;

The originalReleaseDate column is needed to find the oldest card. The rarity column is needed to filter for mythic cards. The format column is needed to identify the legal play formats. The status column is needed to filter for legal formats. The cards.id is needed to join with legalities. Note: id, availability, cardKingdomId, colorIdentity, duelDeck, faceName, frameEffects, hasNonFoil, isPromo, layout, life, name, number, originalText, originalType, scryfallId, scryfallOracleId, side, text, toughness, type, variations are not needed for this query.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1."originalReleaseDate", T2."format"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
  ON T1."id" = T2."id"
WHERE T1."id" = (
  SELECT "id"
  FROM "cards"
  WHERE "rarity" = 'mythic'
  ORDER BY "originalReleaseDate" ASC NULLS LAST
  LIMIT 1
)
AND T2."status" = 'Legal';

The cards table is needed to find the artist and the legalities table is needed to find the format.

The question asks for the illustrator (artist) who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of play for those cards. To achieve this, I need to: 
1. Count the number of cards illustrated by each artist. This requires the `cards` table and its `artist` column.
2. Identify the artist with the minimum count. This involves using the `MIN` aggregate function on the count of cards per artist.
3. Retrieve the formats of play for the cards illustrated by this artist. This requires joining the `cards` table with the `legalities` table on the card's unique identifier (implicitly `uuid` as per schema, though not explicitly stated in the question's context, it's the standard way to link cards to their legalities) and filtering by the identified artist. The `legalities` table has the `format` column.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.artist IN (
    SELECT
      artist
    FROM cards
    GROUP BY
      artist
    HAVING
      COUNT(id) = (
        SELECT
          COUNT(id)
        FROM cards
        GROUP BY
          artist
        ORDER BY
          COUNT(id) ASC
        LIMIT 1
      )
  );

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards. 2) Find the format of play for each card illustrated by that artist. The artist column is needed to find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards. The format column is needed to find the format of play for the cards illustrated by the artist. The cards table is needed to find the artist and the legalities table is needed to find the format.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1."artist",
  T2."format"
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."artist" IN (
    SELECT
      "artist"
    FROM cards
    GROUP BY
      "artist"
    HAVING
      COUNT(*) = (
        SELECT
          MIN(card_count)
        FROM (
          SELECT
            COUNT(*) AS card_count
          FROM cards
          GROUP BY
            "artist"
        ) AS sub_counts
      )
  )
ORDER BY
  T1."artist",
  T2."format";

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards. 2) Find the format of play for each card illustrated by that artist. The artist column is needed to find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards. The format column is needed to find the format of play for the cards illustrated by the artist. The cards table is needed to find the artist and the legalities table is needed to find the format.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist = (SELECT artist FROM cards WHERE artist IS NOT NULL GROUP BY artist ORDER BY COUNT(id) ASC LIMIT 1)

【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810, 6241, 29566]),
(artist:TEXT, Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art., Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet, Matthew D. Wilson, Rebecca Guay]),
(asciiName:TEXT, Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters., Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan, Ghazban Ogre]),
(availability:TEXT, Description: A list of the card's available printing types. Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena, arena,mtgo,paper, arena,paper]),
(borderColor:TEXT, Description: The color of the card border. Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless, silver, gold]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, Description: card Kingdom Foil Id Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096, 123097]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, Description: card Kingdom Id Value Explanation: A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725, 122726, 122727]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text, Examples: [W, B, U, R, G]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types)., Examples: [U, G, R, B]),
(colors:TEXT, Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator. Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U, R, G]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property. Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0, 1.0, 6.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, Description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in., Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, Description: The card rank on EDHRec, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081, 12901, 3988]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, Description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card. Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 3.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, Description: The name on the face of the card., Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit, Memory]),
(flavorName:TEXT, Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function. Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),
(flavorText:TEXT, Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function. Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.),
(frameEffects:TEXT, Description: The visual frame effects. Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc", Examples: [legendary, nyxtouched, miracle, devoid]),
(frameVersion:TEXT, Description: The version of the card frame style. Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future", Examples: [2003, 1993, 2015, 1997, future]),
(hand:TEXT, Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier. Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size => +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size => -1, .... neural maximum hand size => 0...., Examples: [1, 0, -2, -1]),
(hasAlternativeDeckLimit:INTEGER, Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck. Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasContentWarning:INTEGER, Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information. Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values., Examples: [0, 1]),

(isFullArt:INTEGER, Description: If the card has full artwork. Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOnlineOnly:INTEGER, Description: If the card is only available in online game variations. Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOversized:INTEGER, Description: If the card is oversized. Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isPromo:INTEGER, Description: If the card is a promotional printing. Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),

schema_representation.execution_plan:
Execution plan: The question asks for the illustrator (artist) who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of play for those cards. To achieve this, I need to: 
1. Count the number of cards illustrated by each artist. This requires the `cards` table and its `artist` column.
2. Identify the artist with the minimum count. This involves using the `MIN` aggregate function on the count of cards per artist.
3. Retrieve the formats of play for the cards illustrated by this artist. This requires joining the `cards` table with the `legalities` table on the card's unique identifier (implicitly `uuid` as per schema, though not explicitly stated in the question's context, it's the standard way to link cards to their legalities) and filtering by the identified artist. The `legalities` table has the `format` column.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T2."format"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE T1."artist" = (
    SELECT "artist"
    FROM "cards"
    GROUP BY "artist"
    ORDER BY COUNT("id") ASC
    LIMIT 1
);

3. Retrieve the formats of play for the cards illustrated by this artist. sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.artist IN (
    SELECT
      artist
    FROM cards
    GROUP BY
      artist
    HAVING
      COUNT(id) = (
        SELECT
          COUNT(id)
        FROM cards
        GROUP BY
          artist
        ORDER BY
          COUNT(id) ASC
        LIMIT 1
      )
  );

CREATE TABLE posts (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post id,
    PostTypeId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the post type,
    AcceptedAnswerId INTEGER -- Column Description: the accepted answer id of the post,
    CreaionDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the post,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: the score of the post,
    ViewCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the view count of the post, Column Value Explanation: Higher view count means the post has higher popularity,
    Body TEXT -- Column Description: the body of the post,
    OwnerUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the owner user,
    LasActivityDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last activity date,
    Title TEXT -- Column Description: the title of the post,
    Tags TEXT -- Column Description: the tag of the post,
    AnswerCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of answers of the post,
    CommentCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of comments of the post,
    FavoriteCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of favorites of the post, Column Value Explanation: more favorite count refers to more valuable posts.,
    LastEditorUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the last editor,
    LastEditDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last edit date,
    CommunityOwnedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the community owned date,
    ParentId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the parent post, Column Value Explanation: If the parent id is null, the post is the root post. Otherwise, the post is the child post of other post.,
    ClosedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the closed date of the post, Column Value Explanation: if ClosedDate is null or empty, it means this post is not well-finished, if CloseDate is not null or empty, it means this post has well-finished.,
    OwnerDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the post owner,
    LastEditorDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the last editor,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_LastEditorUserId FOREIGN KEY (LastEditorUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_OwnerUserId FOREIGN KEY (OwnerUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_ParentId FOREIGN KEY (ParentId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE users (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the user id,
    Reputation INTEGER -- Column Description: the user's reputation, Column Value Explanation: The user with higher reputation has more influence.,
    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the user account,
    DisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the user's display name,
    LastAccessDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last access date of the user account,
    WebsiteUrl TEXT -- Column Description: the website url of the user account,
    Location TEXT -- Column Description: user's location,
    AboutMe TEXT -- Column Description: the self introduction of the user,
    Views INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of views,
    UpVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of upvotes,
    DownVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of downvotes,
    AccountId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id of the account,
    Age INTEGER -- Column Description: user's age, Column Value Explanation: teenager: 13-18 / adult: 19-65 /elder: > 65,
    ProfileImageUrl TEXT -- Column Description: the profile image url,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id)

);

The posts.Title column is needed to filter for posts mentioning 'variance'. The votes.BountyAmount column is needed to filter for bounty amount of 50. The question asks to identify the user who added a bounty of 50 to a post with 'variance' in its title. To answer this, I need to: 
1. Filter posts by title containing 'variance'. The `posts` table has a `Title` column for this.
2. Filter votes by `BountyAmount` equal to 50. The `votes` table has a `BountyAmount` column.
3. Link the votes to the posts to ensure the bounty is on the correct post.
4. Link the votes to the users to get the user's display name. The `users` table has a `DisplayName` column.
Therefore, I need `posts.Title`, `votes.BountyAmount`, `votes.PostId`, `votes.UserId`, and `users.DisplayName`.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1.DisplayName
FROM users AS T1
INNER JOIN votes AS T2
  ON T1.Id = T2.UserId
INNER JOIN posts AS T3
  ON T2.PostId = T3.Id
WHERE
  T2.BountyAmount = 50 AND T3.Title LIKE '%variance%';

    CreaionDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the post,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: the score of the post,
    ViewCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the view count of the post, Column Value Explanation: Higher view count means the post has higher popularity,
    Body TEXT -- Column Description: the body of the post,
    OwnerUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the owner user,
    LasActivityDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last activity date,
    Title TEXT -- Column Description: the title of the post,
    Tags TEXT -- Column Description: the tag of the post,
    AnswerCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of answers of the post,
    CommentCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of comments of the post,
    FavoriteCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of favorites of the post, Column Value Explanation: more favorite count refers to more valuable posts.,
    LastEditorUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the last editor,
    LastEditDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last edit date,
    CommunityOwnedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the community owned date,
    ParentId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the parent post, Column Value Explanation: If the parent id is null, the post is the root post. Otherwise, the post is the child post of other post.,
    ClosedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the closed date of the post, Column Value Explanation: if ClosedDate is null or empty, it means this post is not well-finished, if CloseDate is not null or empty, it means this post has well-finished.,
    OwnerDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the post owner,
    LastEditorDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the last editor,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_LastEditorUserId FOREIGN KEY (LastEditorUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_OwnerUserId FOREIGN KEY (OwnerUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_ParentId FOREIGN KEY (ParentId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE users (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the user id,
    Reputation INTEGER -- Column Description: the user's reputation, Column Value Explanation: The user with higher reputation has more influence.,
    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the user account,
    DisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the user's display name,
    LastAccessDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last access date of the user account,
    WebsiteUrl TEXT -- Column Description: the website url of the user account,
    Location TEXT -- Column Description: user's location,
    AboutMe TEXT -- Column Description: the self introduction of the user,
    Views INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of views,
    UpVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of upvotes,
    DownVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of downvotes,
    AccountId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id of the account,
    Age INTEGER -- Column Description: user's age, Column Value Explanation: teenager: 13-18 / adult: 19-65 /elder: > 65,
    ProfileImageUrl TEXT -- Column Description: the profile image url,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE votes (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the vote id,
    PostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the post that is voted,
    VoteTypeId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the vote type,
    CreationDate DATE -- Column Description: the creation date of the vote,
    UserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the voter,
    BountyAmount INTEGER -- Column Description: the amount of bounty,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_votes_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_votes_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

Since the question asks for superheroes with over 15 super powers, I need to join the tables that connect superheroes and powers. 2) Filter the results to include only those superheroes with more than 15 powers. 3) Display the full names of the superheroes that meet the criteria. The hero_power table connects superheroes to their powers. The superhero table contains the full_name of the superhero. The superpower table is not needed because the question asks to count the number of powers, not the power names themselves.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1."full_name"
FROM superhero AS T1
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    "hero_id",
    COUNT(*) AS power_count
  FROM hero_power
  GROUP BY
    "hero_id"
  HAVING
    COUNT(*) > 15
) AS T2
ON T1."id" = T2."hero_id";

CREATE TABLE hero_power (

    hero_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the hero Maps to superhero(id),
    power_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the power Maps to superpower(id), Column Value Explanation: In general, a superhero's attributes provide the foundation for their abilities and help to define who they are, while their powers are the specific abilities that they use to fight crime and protect others.,
    CONSTRAINT fk_hero_power_hero_id FOREIGN KEY (hero_id) REFERENCES superhero (id)

);

CREATE TABLE superhero (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the unique identifier of the superhero,
    superhero_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the name of the superhero,
    full_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the full name of the superhero, Column Value Explanation: The full name of a person typically consists of their given name, also known as their first name or personal name, and their surname, also known as their last name or family name. For example, if someone's given name is "John" and their surname is "Smith," their full name would be "John Smith.",
    gender_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's gender,
    eye_colour_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's eye color,
    hair_colour_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's hair color,
    skin_colour_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's skin color,
    race_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's race,
    publisher_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the publisher,
    alignment_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's alignment,
    height_cm INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the height of the superhero, Column Value Explanation: The unit of height is centimeter. If the height_cm is NULL or 0, it means the height of the superhero is missing.,
    weight_kg INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the weight of the superhero, Column Value Explanation: The unit of weight is kilogram. If the weight_kg is NULL or 0, it means the weight of the superhero is missing.,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

This requires joining the results, drivers, and races tables. I need to filter the results by Hamilton's surname and the year of the race. I also need to filter the driver standings by positionText = '1'. The raceId is needed for counting races. The surname is needed to filter by Hamilton. The year is needed to filter by the year since 2010. The positionText is needed to filter the races where Hamilton was not at the 1st track.

The question asks for a percentage of races where Hamilton was not in 1st place since 2010. This requires counting races for Hamilton since 2010 where his position was greater than 1 (numerator) and dividing it by the total count of races for Hamilton since 2010 (denominator). To achieve this, I need to join the `drivers` table (to filter by surname 'Hamilton') with the `results` table (to get the raceId, driverId, and position) and the `races` table (to filter by year). The `driverStandings` table is also relevant as it contains the `positionText` which can be used to identify the 1st position. However, the evidence explicitly mentions 'position' which is available in the `results` table, and the criteria also refers to 'position > 1'. Therefore, `results.position` is the most direct column to use for filtering positions.

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH HamiltonRaces AS (
  SELECT
    T1.raceId,
    T1.position
  FROM driverStandings AS T1
  INNER JOIN drivers AS T2
    ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId
  INNER JOIN races AS T3
    ON T1.raceId = T3.raceId
  WHERE
    T2.surname = 'Hamilton' AND T3.year >= 2010
)
SELECT
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN HR.position > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(HR.raceId)
FROM HamiltonRaces AS HR;

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE circuits (

    circuitId INTEGER -- Column Description: unique identification number of the circuit,
    circuitRef TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' -- Column Description: circuit reference name,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    location TEXT,
    country TEXT,
    lat REAL,
    lng REAL,
    alt INTEGER,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (circuitId)

);

CREATE TABLE drivers (

    driverId INTEGER,
    driverRef TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    number INTEGER,
    code TEXT,
    forename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    surname TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    dob DATE,
    nationality TEXT,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (driverId)

);

CREATE TABLE races (

    raceId INTEGER,
    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    round INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_races_circuitId FOREIGN KEY (circuitId) REFERENCES circuits (circuitId)

);

CREATE TABLE results (

    resultId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique identification number identifying race result,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: the identification number identifying the race,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    number INTEGER,
    grid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    positionOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    laps INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    time TEXT,
    milliseconds INTEGER,
    fastestLap INTEGER,
    rank INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    fastestLapTime TEXT,
    fastestLapSpeed TEXT,
    statusId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (resultId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_driverId FOREIGN KEY (driverId) REFERENCES drivers (driverId)

);

SELECT
  (
    (MAX(T2."milliseconds") - MIN(T2."milliseconds")) * 100.0 / MAX(T2."milliseconds")
  )
FROM races AS T1
INNER JOIN results AS T2
  ON T1."raceId" = T2."raceId"
WHERE
  T1."year" = 2008 AND T1."name" LIKE '%Australian Grand Prix%' AND T2."time" IS NOT NULL;

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE races (

    raceId INTEGER,
    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    round INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE results (

    resultId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique identification number identifying race result,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: the identification number identifying the race,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    number INTEGER,
    grid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    positionOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    laps INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    time TEXT,
    milliseconds INTEGER,
    fastestLap INTEGER,
    rank INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    fastestLapTime TEXT,
    fastestLapSpeed TEXT,
    statusId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (resultId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId)

);

WITH ConvertedTimes AS (
  SELECT
    T1."raceId",
    T2."position",
    (CAST(SUBSTR(T2."time", 1, 2) AS REAL) * 3600 +
     CAST(SUBSTR(T2."time", 4, 2) AS REAL) * 60 +
     CAST(SUBSTR(T2."time", 7, 6) AS REAL)) AS "total_seconds"
  FROM races AS T1
  INNER JOIN results AS T2
    ON T1."raceId" = T2."raceId"
  WHERE
    T1."year" = 2008 AND T2."time" IS NOT NULL
    -- Assumption: The schema does not allow identifying "Australian Grand Prix" specifically.
    -- We select the first raceId found in 2008 as a proxy for the target race.
    AND T1."raceId" = (
      SELECT
        "raceId"
      FROM races
      WHERE
        "year" = 2008
      LIMIT 1
    )
)
SELECT
  ((last_driver."total_seconds" - champion."total_seconds") - champion."total_seconds") * 100.0 / last_driver."total_seconds"
FROM (
  SELECT
    "total_seconds"
  FROM ConvertedTimes
  WHERE
    "position" = 1

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE circuits (

    circuitId INTEGER -- Column Description: unique identification number of the circuit,
    circuitRef TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' -- Column Description: circuit reference name,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    location TEXT,
    country TEXT,
    lat REAL,
    lng REAL,
    alt INTEGER,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (circuitId)

);

CREATE TABLE races (

    raceId INTEGER,
    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    round INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_races_year FOREIGN KEY (year) REFERENCES seasons (year),
    CONSTRAINT fk_races_circuitId FOREIGN KEY (circuitId) REFERENCES circuits (circuitId)

);

CREATE TABLE results (

    resultId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique identification number identifying race result,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: the identification number identifying the race,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    number INTEGER,
    grid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    positionOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    laps INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    time TEXT,
    milliseconds INTEGER,
    fastestLap INTEGER,
    rank INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    fastestLapTime TEXT,
    fastestLapSpeed TEXT,
    statusId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (resultId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE seasons (

    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (year)

);

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE constructorStandings (

    constructorStandingsId INTEGER,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: how many points acquired in each race,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT,
    wins INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (constructorStandingsId)

);

CREATE TABLE driverStandings (

    driverStandingsId INTEGER,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT,
    wins INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: wins,
    PRIMARY KEY (driverStandingsId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_driverStandings_driverId FOREIGN KEY (driverId) REFERENCES drivers (driverId)

);

CREATE TABLE drivers (

    driverId INTEGER,
    driverRef TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    number INTEGER,
    code TEXT,
    forename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    surname TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    dob DATE,
    nationality TEXT,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (driverId)

);

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for drivers born after 1975 who have been ranked 2. The birth year is in the 'drivers' table, and the ranking is in the 'constructorStandings' table. We need to filter drivers by birth year, find their rankings, and filter for a ranking of 2. The 'drivers' table contains the birth year (dob) and the driver's forename and surname. The 'constructorStandings' table contains the positionText. The 'driverStandings' table contains driverId and raceId which is needed to join tables.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1."forename",
  T1."surname"
FROM drivers AS T1
INNER JOIN driverStandings AS T2
  ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId"
INNER JOIN constructorStandings AS T3
  ON T2."raceId" = T3."raceId"
WHERE
  T3."positionText" = '2';

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE driverStandings (

    driverStandingsId INTEGER,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT,
    wins INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: wins,
    PRIMARY KEY (driverStandingsId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_driverStandings_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_driverStandings_driverId FOREIGN KEY (driverId) REFERENCES drivers (driverId)

);

CREATE TABLE drivers (

    driverId INTEGER,
    driverRef TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    number INTEGER,
    code TEXT,
    forename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    surname TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    dob DATE,
    nationality TEXT,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (driverId)

);

CREATE TABLE races (

    raceId INTEGER,
    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    round INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId)

);

The date column is needed for filtering by year. The buildUpPlayPassing column is needed for the average calculation and filtering. The team_api_id is needed to join the Team_Attributes and Team tables. The team_long_name column is needed for output. Note: buildUpPlayDribbling, buildUpPlayDribblingClass, buildUpPlayPassingClass, buildUpPlayPositioningClass, chanceCreationPassing, defencePressure, defenceAggression, defenceTeamWidthClass, and defenceDefenderLineClass are NOT needed for this query.

The question asks for the long name of teams with above-average build-up play passing in 2012. 
1. To get the team's long name, I need to select `team_long_name` from the `Team` table.
2. The build-up play passing information is available in the `Team_Attributes` table, specifically the `buildUpPlayPassing` column. This column needs to be filtered for values above average.
3. The condition 'in 2012' requires filtering based on the `date` column in the `Team_Attributes` table.
4. To calculate the average build-up play passing, I need the sum and count of `buildUpPlayPassing` from `Team_Attributes` for the year 2012, ensuring `buildUpPlayPassing` is not null.
5. Therefore, I need `Team.team_long_name`, `Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing`, and `Team_Attributes.date`.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1."team_long_name"
FROM "Team" AS T1
INNER JOIN "Team_Attributes" AS T2
  ON T1."team_api_id" = T2."team_api_id"
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2."date") = '2012' AND T2."buildUpPlayPassing" IS NOT NULL AND T2."buildUpPlayPassing" > (
    SELECT
      AVG(T3."buildUpPlayPassing")
    FROM "Team_Attributes" AS T3
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', T3."date") = '2012' AND T3."buildUpPlayPassing" IS NOT NULL
  );

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter the Team_Attributes table for the year 2012, 2) Calculate the average buildUpPlayPassing, 3) Filter for teams whose buildUpPlayPassing is above the average, 4) Retrieve the team_long_name from the Team table for the filtered teams. The date column is needed for filtering by year. The buildUpPlayPassing column is needed for the average calculation and filtering. The team_api_id is needed to join the Team_Attributes and Team tables. The team_long_name column is needed for output. Note: buildUpPlayDribbling, buildUpPlayDribblingClass, buildUpPlayPassingClass, buildUpPlayPositioningClass, chanceCreationPassing, defencePressure, defenceAggression, defenceTeamWidthClass, and defenceDefenderLineClass are NOT needed for this query.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1."team_long_name"
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1."team_api_id" = T2."team_api_id"
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2."date") = '2012' AND T2."buildUpPlayPassing" > (
    SELECT
      AVG(T3."buildUpPlayPassing")
    FROM Team_Attributes AS T3
    WHERE

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE Team (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for teams,
    team_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team api,
    team_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team fifa api,
    team_long_name TEXT -- Column Description: the team's long name,
    team_short_name TEXT -- Column Description: the team's short name,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Team_Attributes (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for teams,
    team_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team fifa api,
    team_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team api,
    date TEXT -- Column Description: Date, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2010-02-22 00:00:00,
    buildUpPlaySpeed INTEGER -- Column Description: the speed in which attacks are put together, Column Value Explanation: the score which is between 1-00 to measure the team's attack speed,
    buildUpPlaySpeedClass TEXT -- Column Description: the speed class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Slow: 1-33, Balanced: 34-66, Fast: 66-100,
    buildUpPlayDribbling INTEGER -- Column Description: the tendency/ frequency of dribbling,
    buildUpPlayDribblingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the dribbling class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning: Little: 1-33, Normal: 34-66, Lots: 66-100,
    buildUpPlayPassing INTEGER -- Column Description: affects passing distance and support from teammates,
    buildUpPlayPassingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the passing class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Short: 1-33, Mixed: 34-66, Long: 66-100,
    buildUpPlayPositioningClass TEXT -- Column Description: A team's freedom of movement in the 1st two thirds of the pitch, Column Value Explanation: Organised / Free Form,
    chanceCreationPassing INTEGER -- Column Description: Amount of risk in pass decision and run support,
    chanceCreationPassingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the chance creation passing class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Safe: 1-33, Normal: 34-66, Risky: 66-100,
    chanceCreationCrossing INTEGER -- Column Description: The tendency / frequency of crosses into the box,
    chanceCreationCrossingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the chance creation crossing class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Little: 1-33, Normal: 34-66, Lots: 66-100,
    chanceCreationShooting INTEGER -- Column Description: The tendency / frequency of shots taken,
    chanceCreationShootingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the chance creation shooting class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Little: 1-33, Normal: 34-66, Lots: 66-100,
    chanceCreationPositioningClass TEXT -- Column Description: A team�s freedom of movement in the final third of the pitch, Column Value Explanation: Organised / Free Form,
    defencePressure INTEGER -- Column Description: Affects how high up the pitch the team will start pressuring,
    defencePressureClass TEXT -- Column Description: the defence pressure class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Deep: 1-33, Medium: 34-66, High: 66-100,
    defenceAggression INTEGER -- Column Description: Affect the team�s approach to tackling the ball possessor,
    defenceAggressionClass TEXT -- Column Description: the defence aggression class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Contain: 1-33, Press: 34-66, Double: 66-100,
    defenceTeamWidth INTEGER -- Column Description: Affects how much the team will shift to the ball side,
    defenceTeamWidthClass TEXT -- Column Description: the defence team width class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Narrow: 1-33, Normal: 34-66, Wide: 66-100,
    defenceDefenderLineClass TEXT -- Column Description: Affects the shape and strategy of the defence, Column Value Explanation: Cover/ Offside Trap,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Team_Attributes_team_api_id FOREIGN KEY (team_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Team_Attributes_team_fifa_api_id FOREIGN KEY (team_fifa_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_fifa_api_id)

);

        WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', "T2"."date") = '2012'

            SELECT AVG("buildUpPlayPassing")

Execution plan: The question asks for the long name of teams with above-average build-up play passing in 2012. 
1. To get the team's long name, I need to select `team_long_name` from the `Team` table.
2. The build-up play passing information is available in the `Team_Attributes` table, specifically the `buildUpPlayPassing` column. This column needs to be filtered for values above average.
3. The condition 'in 2012' requires filtering based on the `date` column in the `Team_Attributes` table.
4. To calculate the average build-up play passing, I need the sum and count of `buildUpPlayPassing` from `Team_Attributes` for the year 2012, ensuring `buildUpPlayPassing` is not null.
5. Therefore, I need `Team.team_long_name`, `Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing`, and `Team_Attributes.date`.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1."team_long_name"
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1."team_api_id" = T2."team_api_id"
WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2."date") = '2012'
  AND T2."buildUpPlayPassing" > (
    SELECT AVG(T3."buildUpPlayPassing")
    FROM Team_Attributes AS T3
    WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T3."date") = '2012' AND T3."buildUpPlayPassing" IS NOT NULL
  );

preliminary_sql:
SELECT
  T1."player_name"
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.player_fifa_api_id = T2.player_fifa_api_id
WHERE
  T1."height" > 180
GROUP BY
  T1."player_name"
ORDER BY
  AVG(T2."heading_accuracy") DESC
LIMIT 10;

The player_name column is needed for the output. The height column is needed to filter players. The heading_accuracy column is needed for the average calculation. The player_fifa_api_id column is needed to group the heading accuracy by player. The player_api_id is needed to join the tables. Note: other columns are NOT needed.

The question asks for the names of the top 10 players whose heights are above 180, ordered by their average heading accuracy in descending order. To achieve this, I need to: 
1. Filter players by height from the 'Player' table.
2. Calculate the average heading accuracy for each player. This requires accessing the 'heading_accuracy' column from the 'Player_Attributes' table and grouping by player.
3. Join the 'Player' and 'Player_Attributes' tables to link player names with their attributes.
4. Order the results by the calculated average heading accuracy in descending order.
5. Limit the results to the top 10.

Therefore, the essential columns are:
- `Player.player_name`: To retrieve the player's name as required by the output.
- `Player.height`: To filter players whose height is above 180.
- `Player_Attributes.heading_accuracy`: To calculate the average heading accuracy.
- `Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id`: To join with the Player table and group by player for calculating the average heading accuracy.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 GROUP BY T1.player_name, T1.player_api_id ORDER BY AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

SELECT T1."player_name"
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1."player_api_id" = T2."player_api_id"
WHERE
  T1."height" > 180
GROUP BY
  T1."player_api_id",
  T1."player_name"
ORDER BY
  AVG(T2."heading_accuracy") DESC
LIMIT 10;

SELECT
  T1."player_name"
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1."player_fifa_api_id" = T2."player_fifa_api_id"
WHERE
  T1."player_name" IN ('Alexis', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone')
ORDER BY
  T2."crossing" DESC
LIMIT 1;

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find the crossing score for each player (Alexis, Ariel Borysiuk, and Arouna Kone) and then determine the maximum crossing score among them. I will need to filter the `Player` table to identify the players by name, then join with `Player_Attributes` to get the crossing scores. The `player_name` column is needed to filter for the specified players. The `crossing` column is needed to determine the best crossing score. The `player_fifa_api_id` is needed to join the tables.

The question asks to identify the player with the best crossing performance among Alexis, Ariel Borysiuk, and Arouna Kone. The 'Player_Attributes' table contains the 'crossing' score, which directly relates to crossing performance. The 'Player' table contains the 'player_name'. To link these two, we need to join them using a common identifier. The 'Player_Attributes' table has 'player_fifa_api_id' which is also present in the 'Player' table (as 'player_fifa_api_id' is a foreign key to Player.player_api_id). We need to filter the players by their names and then find the maximum crossing score among them. Finally, we need to return the player's name associated with that maximum score.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN (SELECT player_api_id, MAX(crossing) AS max_crossing FROM Player_Attributes GROUP BY player_api_id) AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.player_name IN ('Alexis', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone') ORDER BY T2.max_crossing DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

SELECT
  T1."player_name"
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1."player_api_id" = T2."player_api_id"
WHERE
  T1."player_name" IN ('Alexis', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone')
GROUP BY
  T1."player_name"
HAVING
  MAX(T2."crossing") = (
    SELECT
      MAX(sub_max_crossing)

      SELECT

      WHERE
        T4."player_name" IN ('Alexis', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone')
      GROUP BY
        T4."player_name"
    )
  );
